# Provider {#sec-provider}

The provider module is found in `backend/core/provider/`. It has two
responsibilities. The family of the backend is recognised, and the noise profile
of a reference machine is chosen. Two files are used: `provider.py` and
`profiles.py`.

## `detect(backend, entangler=None)` {.unnumbered}

The main function of the module. The provider, the entangler and the noise
profile of a backend are returned together in one `BackendInfo` object.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | any object | required | The backend that is injected by Qollab, or a local backend in a test. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` or `None` | `None` | The target entangler. When it is `None`, the entangler is inferred from the backend and from its name. |

**Returns** a `BackendInfo` object. See the [Data model](model.qmd) page for its
fields.

## How the entangler is chosen {.unnumbered}

The following order is used. The first step that gives an answer is kept.

1. **The parameter.** When `entangler` is given, it is used as it is.
2. **The backend itself.** When the backend advertises only one native
   two-qubit gate, that gate is used. For example, a backend whose operation
   names contain `zz` but not `ms` gives `"zz"`.
3. **The machine family.** The family is read from the name. A name that
   contains `forte` or `ideal` gives `"zz"`. A name that contains `aria` gives
   `"ms"`.
4. **The default.** When nothing is found, `"ms"` is used.

A name that contains `ideal` is treated as a `zz` machine, because the ideal
reference is paired with the fixed `zz` entangler.

## How the hardware flag is set {.unnumbered}

`is_hardware` is `True` only for an IonQ backend that is not a simulator. A
boolean attribute of the backend is preferred, because it is set by the software
development kit itself. The attributes `_simulator`, `_is_simulator`,
`is_simulator` and `simulator` are checked, in this order.

The name is inspected only as a last resort, when no attribute is found. This is
deliberate. A name is a weak signal, and it can be misleading. The attribute is
always preferred when it exists.

## `detect_provider(backend)` {.unnumbered}

The family of the backend is found, and one of the five provider names is
returned.

**Parameter**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | any object | The backend to classify. |

**Returns** one of `"ionq"`, `"ibm"`, `"aws"`, `"local"` or `"unknown"`.

The detection is layered. The reliable signals are checked first, and a
structural fallback is used last.

### The first signals {.unnumbered}

| Signal | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| the class module starts with `qiskit_ionq`, or the name contains `ionq` | `ionq` |
| the module is `qiskit_ibm_runtime`, the name starts with `fake_` or `ibm_`, the class is `GenericBackendV2`, or the module contains `ibm` | `ibm` |
| the module starts with `qiskit_braket_provider`, or the name contains `braket` | `aws` |
| the name or the class contains `BasicSimulator` or `aer_simulator` | `local` |

### The structural fallback {.unnumbered}

When the signals above give no answer, the operation names that the backend
advertises are inspected. They are read from `target.operation_names`, from
`operation_names`, or from `configuration().basis_gates`.

| Operation names that are found | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| any of `gpi`, `gpi2`, `ms`, `zz` | `ionq` |
| `ecr` | `ibm` |
| `cz`, `sx` and `rz` together | `ibm` |
| any of `rxx`, `ryy` | `ionq` |
| anything else | `unknown` |

This fallback exists so that a backend with an unusual name, but with a clear
gate set, is still classified correctly. An unknown provider is never an error,
because the generic translator is used for it.

## The noise profiles {.unnumbered}

The file `profiles.py` contains three ready-made profiles.

| Constant | Machine | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARIA` | IonQ Aria | Used for the MS entangler. |
| `FORTE` | IonQ Forte | Used for the ZZ entangler. |
| `IDEAL` | an ideal machine | All fidelities are 1, and all prices are 0. |

The numbers are simple estimates that were taken from public IonQ material. They
are **not** a calibrated noise model. They can be replaced before the demo.

## `get_profile(machine)` {.unnumbered}

A profile is returned by its short name.

**Parameter**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | string | One of `"aria"`, `"forte"` or `"ideal"`. |

**Returns** a `NoiseProfile`.

## `profile_for(provider, name, entangler)` {.unnumbered}

The correct profile is chosen for a backend.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | The provider name. |
| `name` | string | The raw backend name. It is used to find `aria`, `forte` or `ideal`. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The fallback entangler when the name gives no hint. |

**Returns** a `NoiseProfile`.

**The rule.** The name is checked first. A name that contains `ideal` gives the
ideal profile, `forte` gives the Forte profile and `aria` gives the Aria profile.
If the name gives no hint, the reference machine of the entangler is used: Aria
for MS and Forte for ZZ. A non-IonQ backend is therefore shown *as if* it ran on
trapped ions.
